div.note: NEA files, lot 59 D 518, “Alpha—Memos, etc., beginning after 2nd London Talks—April 26–June 30, ‘55”
div.head:
No. 920
Aide-Mémoire From the Department of State to the British Embassy
div.p:
The Department of State welcomes the suggestion of Sir Anthony Eden that the United States and United Kingdom renew efforts to develop policies designed to ease Arab-Israel tensions and bring about a lasting settlement. The entire problem, which is giving the Department of State constant concern despite some general improvement of conditions in the area, is under active study here and
the Department of State looks forward to a comprehensive discussion with the Foreign Office. The Department of State would prefer to hold the talks immediately after the New Year, which would facilitate completion of its review, and it would be agreeable to sending officers to London for the purpose. The mechanism which should be used to carry out the project could be determined during the consultations in London.

The Department of State does not believe it necessary to advise other countries of the plans at this stage. Eventually, it may prove useful to keep both the French and Turks generally informed, and perhaps to solicit their assistance in connection with certain aspects of the undertaking.

note.p: At this point in the source text, an unknown hand inserted brackets around the phrase “immediately after the New Year,” and substituted the phrase: “about the middle of January, 1955”.
